MIND. [1] [Eup. pur.]
Stupid, dull. θ Dropsy. θ Intermittent.
Moaning ; suffering expressed by peculiar cries.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Eup. pur.]
Head feels light and dizzy, as though flying round and round ; cannot get rid of the sensation as if falling towards the left side ; the whole body seems to participate.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Eup. pur.]
Dull, heavy pain in head ; most severe in forehead.
Much headache and constriction over frontal region, with chill.
Head feels as though she had a bad cold.
Violent headache : before the chill ; during morning ; with fever.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Eup. pur.]
Soreness, tenderness, and itching of scalp.
Sweat, principally on head, particularly profuse about forehead.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Eup. pur.]
Staring ; looking with fixed eyes, wide open.
Copious flow of tears, filling eyes, making constant wiping necessary.
Eyes red and swollen ; violent headache.
Conjunctiva yellow, with the chill.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Eup. pur.]
Ears feel as though they were full.
Crackling, like burning of birch-bark ; very much < upon swallowing anything.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Eup. pur.]
Fluent coryza ; great heat, sneezing.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Eup. pur.]
Face flushed, with fever.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Eup. pur.]
Lips blue. θ Intermittent.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Eup. pur.]
Tongue furred, brown along centre ; bitter, pappy taste, with chill.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Eup. pur.]
Choking fulness of throat, must swallow often.
Swallowing : < crackling in ears ; causes pain.
Continued smarting and burning, most severe in posterior part of throat.
Pain in left side of throat, causing pain in swallowing ; before chill.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Eup. pur.]
Thirst before the chill, none during.
Constant thirst with fever.
Thirst, in a case of dropsy.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Eup. pur.]
Great nausea and sickness of stomach, but no vomiting with the chill.
Nausea ; vomiting with fever.
Vomiting, with sick headache.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Eup. pur.]
Crampy pain in stomach ; gnawing and sighing.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Eup. pur.]
Rumbling, rolling, and twisting pain in bowels.
Severe colic pain over whole abdomen, after voiding urine.
Hypogastric region swollen and hot. θ Suppression of urine.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Eup. pur.]
Bowels inclined to be loose. θ Intermittent.
Bilious diarrhœa.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Eup. pur.]
Dull, deep pain in kidneys ; also cutting pain.
Chronic nephritis.
Suppression of urine.
Smarting and burning very intense in bladder and urethra, so much so that she could not stand.
Severe, deep, dull aching in bladder.
Chronic irritation of bladder, with increased mucous secretion.
Excessive irritation of bladder, with large deposits of lithates.
Uneasiness in region of bladder while suffering from a violent cold ; continued to increase until it became a confirmed chronic inflammation.
Incontinence of urine ; especially with children.
Restless tossing about ; constant moaning, expressed by peculiar cries ; lower belly swollen and hot.
Violent headache, soreness all over, aching, gnawing in joints ; eyes red and swollen ; violent cutting pain in back ; labor-like pains in back ; constant desire to void urine ; most excruciating, smarting and burning in urethra upon voiding urine ; passes a few drops at a time, and is obliged to make the effort very often ; numbness of legs ; deep, dull aching in kidneys ; also in bladder ; great emaciation ; hectic fever ; night sweats ; rheumatic pains shifting from place to place. θ Chronic cystitis.
Catarrh vesica, attended by ulceration.
After riding four miles a very rough road, with much jolting and shaking, seven months pregnant, and taking a bad cold, violent dysuria.
Strangury, due to uterine displacement.
Ischuria with child two weeks old.
Passes a few drops of urine at a time, and is obliged to make the effort very often.
Urine scanty, albuminous, and frequent.
Renal and vesical calculi.
Dysuria, enuresis nocturna, and other conditions of irritation of bladder from direct or reflex causes.
Vesical irritability in women.
   

MALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [22] [Eup. pur.]
Impotency, from exhaustion or abuse of the generative functions.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Eup. pur.]
Sterility, from atony of ovaries.
Uterine leucorrhœa caused by exhaustion of uterus and chronic metritis.
The external generative organs feel as though wet, though a delusion.
Inflammation of meatus urinarius.
Numbness, worse in groin.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Eup. pur.]
Threatened abortion.
Habitual abortion at third or fourth month.
Insufficient labor pains.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Eup. pur.]
Difficult breathing ; distressing dyspnœa.
Grating sensation in chest at every deep inspiration.
   

COUGH. [27] [Eup. pur.]
Spell of dry, hacking cough previous to attack, continuing throughout paroxysm.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Eup. pur.]
Pulse accelerated and full. θ Ague.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Eup. pur.]
Between shoulder blades chilly feeling.
Violent cutting pain in back.
Labor-like pains in back.
Chill begins in lower dorsal region and runs up the back.
Neuralgic pains from below upwards, mostly left side of back and hip.
Distressing pain in lumbar region before chill.
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Eup. pur.]
Arms perspire most ; hands are cold ; finger-nails blue.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Eup. pur.]
Gnawing in hip-bone.
Thighs perspiring most ; feet cold.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Eup. pur.]
Rheumatic pains shifting from place to place, always from below upwards.
Pains in arms and legs before chill.
Limbs cold, during fever.
   

NERVES. [36] [Eup. pur.]
Restlessness, tossing, constant moaning.
Unable to lie down.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Eup. pur.]
Yawning, gaping, sighing.
Sleep restless and much disturbed, frightful dreams.
   

FEVER. [40] [Eup. pur.]
Chilly down back, when changing position ever so little.
General coldness of whole body.
Chill begins in small of back, and spreads over body ; violent shaking, with comparatively little coldness ; bone pains ; thirst in chill and heat ; nails blue.
Skin hot and dry with fever ; hot to touch in face.
Fever protracted, with bone pains, nausea and vomiting, followed by slight sweat, mostly about forehead and head.
Sweat : principally about forehead ; chilly when attempting to shift position.
Hectic fever, with night sweats ; pulse feeble but regular.
Pulse ranged from 80 to 100 ; full and bounding.
Chill commences in small of back and extends from this point up and down body simultaneously ; slightest movement while covered, or draft of air blowing upon patient, produces a transient return of chill after it has apparently passed away, and after the fever has set in ; this is also the case during the sweat, but not so marked severe bone pains. θ Intermittent fever.
During morning, headache, pain in lumbar region, arms, legs, and left side of throat ; after 3 P. M., chilly feeling in lumbar region, extending up as far as between shoulder blades, cold hands and feet, finger-nails blue, general coldness ; after from one to three hours, fever, flushed face, suffused eyes, lachrymation, running at nose ; constant thirst ; desire for cold and acid drinks ; loss of appetite ; restless sleep, with frightful dreams.
At 10 A. M., every other day, begins to yawn, gape, stretch out, and then to shake ; coldness appears to commence about trunk first, while hands and feet become so in half or three-quarters of an hour afterwards ; finger and toe-nails become blue ; child does not shake continually during the chill, but appears to shudder at intervals for a moment or so ; after two hours slight fever with thirst, both continuing about an hour and followed by perspiration, particularly about upper portion of body. θ Quotidian intermittent.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Eup. pur.]
Distressing dyspnœa ; whole body and extremities extremely œdematous ; secretion of urine very scanty, only 3 or 4 ounces in twenty-four hours ; no organic disease discernible ; urine however slightly albuminous ; pulse feeble but regular ; extremities cold ; considerable general prostration. θ Dropsy.
